seo.title: Our approach
seo.description: Person first, wellness first. How Boulder Feet Forward meets people where they are.

fields.lead: No single solution fits every individual. We help each person find the one that works for them.
fields.title: A different way to reach people.

items.text: Our care is collaborative, trust-based, trauma-informed and built on choice. The individual determines the destination.
items.title: Person first

items.text: We don’t decide that everyone needs treatment first, housing first, employment first or sobriety first. We ask: what does success look like to you, and what would it take to make that happen?
items.title: Wellness first

items.text: We don’t duplicate the larger system of care. We extend its reach. We work alongside existing providers and care teams so people can get services they might otherwise never reach.
items.title: The engagement bridge

content.text: Our framework is SAMHSA’s Eight Dimensions of Wellness. People need support in every one of them, not just one. Choose a dimension to see how our work touches it, from the first conversation to the long haul.

dimensions.name: Emotional
dimensions.step1: Daily connection and a co-equal relationship with peers
dimensions.step2: Care referrals, and our continued daily presence
dimensions.summary: Wellbeing starts with someone who shows up. Our peers are there every day, as equals.

dimensions.name: Occupational
dimensions.step1: Reliable transportation (bus passes, bike locks) and professional clothing
dimensions.step2: Referrals for job placement programs, and résumé assistance
dimensions.summary: Work and purpose depend on being able to get there, and to show up as yourself.

dimensions.name: Intellectual
dimensions.step1: Art, poetry and movie workshops, and supplies
dimensions.step2: Exploration: referrals and information for classes, groups and events
dimensions.step3: Program enrollments for education and more, with ongoing goal-setting and support
dimensions.summary: Curiosity doesn't wait for housing. Learning is part of how people rebuild.

dimensions.name: Environmental
dimensions.step1: Park cleanup, sleeping bags or blankets, clothing
dimensions.step2: Laundry vouchers, plus referrals and information for shelters and free, friendly public spaces with bathrooms, showers and storage
dimensions.summary: The spaces people live in, and move through, shape everything else.

dimensions.name: Financial
dimensions.step2: Enrollment and advocacy for Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND), SSI and SSDI
dimensions.step3: Long-term goal setting and individualized planning
dimensions.summary: Money is a barrier at every step. We remove it first, then help people build a way forward.

dimensions.name: Social
dimensions.step2: Continued daily interaction, deepening connection, and prosocial events
dimensions.summary: Belonging is basic. It starts with conversation and grows into community.

dimensions.name: Physical
dimensions.step1: Nutritious food and water, hygiene supplies, basic wound care, safe-use and harm reduction supplies, and safer-sex supplies
dimensions.step2: Food bank information, care referrals, and SNAP and Medicaid enrollment
dimensions.summary: Food, water, first aid and harm reduction come first, wherever someone is.

dimensions.name: Spiritual
dimensions.step1: Outreach by the faith groups that join our events
dimensions.step2: Conversation, and referrals to programs and groups that fit each person
dimensions.summary: Meaning looks different for everyone. We make room for whatever it is for you.

content.text: Every dimension has three levels of support. We start with what is in front of us, and we build from there.

items.text: Plan an accessible solution someone can use for themselves.
items.title: Stabilizing resources

fields.heading: What meeting people where they are looks like.

items.text: Nutritious meals, hygiene supplies, clothing and weather gear, first aid, harm reduction supplies, pet care supplies and more. We provide the infrastructure, food and hygiene supplies. Partners, volunteers and donors expand what is on the table, and providers get a reliable place to meet people who may never walk through their doors.
items.title: Twice a week, zero-barrier outreach events

items.text: A bus pass, a bike lock, glasses, laundry, a shower, a haircut, a bike or car repair, a safe place to park, a phone call. If the resource exists, we help people reach it, and we spend our own dollars only where we find gaps. It is whatever small thing is standing between someone and their next step.
items.title: We solve the problem in front of us

items.text: Coordinated Entry from wherever you are. Housing assessments on site. IDs and documents, social benefits, health and behavioral health care, employment, education and volunteer opportunities, legal resources, treatment, sober living and many pathways to recovery. Trained peers help with applications, phone calls, paperwork, rides and the next step.
items.title: We help people navigate services and systems

items.text: We introduce people to providers, help them through intake, advocate when needed, get them to appointments, follow up afterward and coordinate with existing care teams. If something does not work, we troubleshoot, try something else and learn from it.
items.title: We make warm handoffs, not just referrals

items.text: Workshops and useful information, art and poetry, movies and games, trauma-informed movement and more. Belonging is part of stability.
items.title: We create connection, community and belonging

fields.heading: We stick around for the long haul.

content.text: We start with daily successes, then help build an individualized path forward. That might mean supportive housing, student housing, family reunification, becoming a live-in caregiver, meaningful employment, finding roommates, or saving for an RV.
There is more than one way home.
